On 30 October 2023, the Council unanimously adopted United Kingdom draft S/2023/808 as resolution 2704 (2023) [VOTE]. The resolution extended the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024 [OPERATIVE]. While resolution 2694 already mandated monitoring of the Government–ELN ceasefire, resolution 2704 expressed willingness to consider Government–EMC verification only upon the Secretary-General confirming a ceasefire with appropriate protocols [ADDITIONAL].

Brazil emphasized Colombia's sovereign will and supported the Government's total peace strategy, hoping the Council could authorize EMC verification when sufficiently mature [BRAZIL]. The African members, speaking on behalf of Ghana, welcomed the unanimous extension and supported EMC monitoring contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions, while pledging to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter [A3].

Both statements support the shared ground that any future verification of the Government–EMC ceasefire must remain strictly conditional on the Secretary-General's confirmation of a ceasefire and the establishment of appropriate verification protocols. This aligns with the resolution's explicit preambular conditions [ADDITIONAL]. The Council thus reaffirmed its commitment to peace while maintaining rigorous procedural safeguards for new ceasefire monitoring.

Cover the draft and vote, the existing mandate extension, the prior and prospective ceasefire verification scopes and any conditions, the two statements from Brazil and the African members, and what shared ground those statements support. Distinguish statements from adopted authority and cite each factual sentence using bracketed source IDs.", "sources": {"VOTE": "S/PV.9461, p. 2. On 30 October 2023, the Council voted on United Kingdom draft S/2023/808. All 15 members voted in favour and the Council President announced unanimous adoption as resolution 2704 (2023).", "OPERATIVE": "Resolution 2704, operative paragraphs 1 and 2. The Council extended the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024. It expressed willingness to work with Colombia's Government on further extension of the mandate on the basis of agreement between the parties.", "ADDITIONAL": "Resolution 2704, final preambular paragraph. Resolution 2694 had already extended the Mission's role to monitoring and verification of the Government–ELN ceasefire. Resolution 2704 expressed willingness to consider Government–EMC monitoring and verification when the Secretary-General confirms a ceasefire with appropriate verification protocols and taking into account his update on implementation of resolution 2694.", "BRAZIL": "S/PV.9461, p. 3. The presiding representative switched to speaking for Brazil. He said the Council should respond to Colombia's priorities as expressed by its Government and described the resolution as reflecting Colombia's sovereign will. Brazil supported the Government's total peace strategy and hoped the Council could authorize verification of the EMC ceasefire when sufficiently mature.", "A3": "S/PV.9461, p. 2. Ghana spoke on behalf of the three African members. The A3 welcomed the unanimous mandate extension, supported Mission monitoring and verification in the EMC case contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions, and pledged to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous people."}, "working_notes": ["**Note 1: Distinction on Mandate Scope and Conditions**\nResolution 2704 (2023) extends the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024 but explicitly conditions the verification of the Government–EMC ceasefire on the Secretary-General confirming a ceasefire with appropriate protocols, distinct from the immediate mandate for the Government–ELN ceasefire established in Resolution 2694. This conditional framework was supported by Brazil, which noted the resolution reflects Colombia's sovereign will and expressed hope that the Council would", "**Note 1: Mandate Extension and Conditional EMC Verification**\nThe A3 statement accurately reflects the source conditions by distinguishing the automatic extension of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024 from the conditional willingness to monitor the Government–EMC ceasefire. As per **S/PV.9461, p. 2** and **Resolution 2704, final preambular paragraph**, the A3 correctly notes that the EMC monitoring is contingent upon the Secretary-General confirming a ceasefire with appropriate verification protocols"]}

output:
On 30 October 2023, the Council unanimously adopted United Kingdom draft S/2023/808 as resolution 2704 (2023) [VOTE]. The resolution extended the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024 [OPERATIVE]. While resolution 2694 mandated monitoring of the Government–ELN ceasefire, resolution 2704 expressed willingness to consider Government–EMC verification only upon the Secretary-General confirming a ceasefire with appropriate protocols [ADDITIONAL].

Brazil stated the resolution reflects Colombia's sovereign will and supported the Government's total peace strategy, hoping the Council would authorize EMC verification when sufficiently mature [BRAZIL]. The African members, speaking on behalf of Ghana, welcomed the unanimous extension and supported EMC monitoring contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions, pledging to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter [A3].

Both statements support the shared ground that the Government–EMC verification mandate is not immediate but conditional. They agree that such verification requires the Secretary-General to confirm a ceasefire with appropriate protocols before the Council authorizes monitoring. This consensus aligns with the resolution's explicit conditions regarding the EMC scope [ADDITIONAL].
